reviewed-card-sha256-algorithm: plain sha256 over the card file bytes at e70565c (git blob 6ce02acbbdb119004c2464b48c1f2b362205245d). NOT the CE canonical digest. Two independent reasons. (1) The check never runs for this card: internal/usecase/task/validator_receipt.go:38 returns early unless zoneFromPath(path) == tasks/done/, and :42 returns early unless blocks: is non-empty; this card is in tasks/doing/ and declares no blocks:, so ce task validate prints no canonical digest to copy. (2) The canonical digest of this card in its present form is not obtainable at all without first adding blocks:, and blocks: is inside the digest subject, so the probe would report a digest of the probe rather than of the card. Measured, not assumed - see independent-verification.seal-preconditions.
digest-scope-warning: This names the revision review-387 actually read: the card's bytes at e70565c. Closing the card will change those bytes - status: doing -> done, the added quality-review* frontmatter, and the move to tasks/done/ - so this filename's sha will not equal a plain sha256 of the committed card. That is expected and is not a defect in this receipt. It is also NOT the h(x) in x self-reference the board had assumed: card_digest.go:22-28 excludes quality-review-receipt from the digest subject precisely so a receipt can name its own card. See independent-verification.digest-convergence-is-achievable. HAZARD AND REMEDY: a plain sha256 can never equal the canonical digest, so if TASK-387 is ever given a blocks: entry and moved to tasks/done/, this pin becomes an unrecoverable hard error. Should that happen, do not re-pin this file - re-issue a receipt whose reviewed-card-sha256 is the CE canonical digest, obtained by finalising the card's other frontmatter and body first, pinning 0, and reading the expected value out of ce task validate's mismatch message. As the card stands (tasks/doing/, no blocks:) the check is unreachable and this pin is a provenance record, not a gate. MEASURED CORRECTION to the hazard above: switching this pin to the CE canonical digest today would NOT remove it. status: and blocks: are both inside the digest subject (probed on TASK-376: changing either alone moves the digest), so a canonical value computed at e70565c breaks at close just as the plain sha256 does. A durable canonical pin can only be taken after the card is finalised, which is a close-time act, not a review-time one. See independent-verification.digest-subject-includes-status-and-blocks.
receipt-path-note: Written under the Git-tracked tasks/receipts/TASK-<N>/ path TASK-383 established and TASK-388 completed the migration to. Self-contained by design: findings and checks-run are inline, with no evidence-path pointer to an untracked file.

digest-convergence-is-achievable.claim-under-review: the board's working conclusion (review-385, echoed by team-lead) that a digest-named receipt can never match its closed card because the filename holds sha256(card) while the card holds the filename - h(x) in x
digest-convergence-is-achievable.result: FALSE as a structural claim, and measurably so.
evidence: card_digest.go:22-28 reviewSubjectExcluded() excludes exactly four keys: quality-review, quality-reviewed-at, quality-review-receipt, review_status. The pointer field is excluded BY DESIGN, and the source comment states the reason: 'the digest has to be computable BEFORE they exist'. The self-reference is solved, not unsolvable.

All four sealed cards on this board converge: TASK-376/377/378/379 each pin a digest that equals their CURRENT closed bytes - ce task validate returns Valid for all four. A thing that happened four times is not impossible.
digest-convergence-is-achievable.actual-cause-of-divergence: quality-review-evidence is deliberately NOT excluded (card_digest.go:17-20), and neither are status:, verification-status: or completion-summary:. So a digest taken before those are written diverges. The source names the remedy: 'an ordering constraint: the evidence must be written before the digest is taken.'
digest-convergence-is-achievable.consequence: The divergences the board measured (TASK-386 9993f021 vs e57dae0d, TASK-388 3edee27d vs fce997be) are procedural, not structural. This matters to ISSUE-001 and to TASK-389, which are currently reasoning from the structural framing.
digest-convergence-is-achievable.concurrent-independent-finding: review-389 reached the same conclusion from the same source in parallel and has already corrected the board's working note. The two measurements were taken independently and agree, including on the detail that quality-review-evidence is the one closing field inside the digest subject. Recorded here as corroboration, not as a separate discovery.

digests-pinned-are-canonical-not-plain.method: compared each pin against shasum -a 256 of the card file
digests-pinned-are-canonical-not-plain.result: CONFIRMED (team-lead's report re-measured independently). 376 pin 9515457848.. vs plain d0e4088c18..; 377 dc496420ce.. vs 9b0957446f..; 378 9d7f1dc95a.. vs 3b83f103b7..; 379 d8827926379.. vs ad71ede7f8... All four DIFFER, yet all four validate Valid. Therefore the pins are CE canonical digests.

digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.question: would pinning the CE canonical digest today make this receipt durable?
digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.answer: No. Neither pin survives, because both fields that would change are inside the digest subject.
digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.method: single-field probes on tasks/done/376-*.md, whose pin currently verifies

probes.result: digests to 933be58f93d0e2c6.. instead of the pinned 9515457848da06f4.. -> status IS inside the subject
digests to 85d154762283b37b.. -> blocks IS inside the subject

digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.consequence: TASK-387 is status: doing with no blocks:. Closing it sets status: done, and any later addition of blocks: is itself a subject change. So a canonical digest computed at e70565c would be stale the moment the card is closed - exactly like the plain sha256, and for the same reason. The choice between the two algorithms today is not a choice between durable and fragile; both are provenance records.
digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.what-actually-produces-a-durable-pin: the ordering the source names (card_digest.go:17-20): finalise status:, quality-review-evidence and the body FIRST, then take the canonical digest. That is a close-time act, and it is how TASK-376/377/378/379 converge. A reviewer cannot perform it, because the evidence being digested is written from the review that is not yet finished.
digest-subject-includes-status-and-block.recommendation: leave this receipt as the record of the reviewed revision, and let the commit that closes TASK-387 issue the canonical pin if the card is ever given blocks:. Do not retro-fit a canonical digest onto the doing-zone card: it would name a revision that never existed in tasks/done/.
